historical_references.reference: Buqrat was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad and one of the Ten Promised Paradise. He was known for his generosity and was given the nickname 'Abu Luttub' because he always carried a large water skin (luttub) to give water to travelers.
historical_references.context: Pre-Islamic Arabia: Buqrat was a well-known figure in pre-Islamic Arabia for his generosity and hospitality to travelers before he embraced Islam and became a companion of the Prophet Muhammad.

historical_references.reference: Buqrat was also a prominent figure in the early Islamic community in Medina and was a key participant in several significant events, including the Battle of Uhud and the Treaty of Hudaybiyah. He was known for his bravery and strong faith, and was highly respected by the Prophet Muhammad and other companions.
historical_references.context: Islamic Medina: Buqrat played an important role in the early Islamic community in Medina and was a respected and courageous companion of the Prophet Muhammad during the formative years of the Islamic state.
